title: The Home Server
tagline: About 40 apps and 48 TB of drives, on one small PC.
what: The computer in my house that everything else leans on. It streams our movies and shows to family and friends, runs the downloads, handles everyone's sign-ins and keeps watch on itself, all from five hard drives pooled into one.
built: Converted the storage drives from a Windows format to a Linux one, over six days
Joined five drives into one 48 TB folder that every device sees as a single drive
Added one Google sign-in button, so family and friends log in without a password from me
credit: I set it up and run it, on top of Docker and Jellyfin

making.problem: I wanted one home for the movie library, downloads and family sign-ins, without tending a separate machine for each.
how: Every app runs in its own container, a sealed-off box, so one broken app can't take down the rest.
The five big drives are joined into one pool, so a movie lives in one place and every device sees one folder.
A single Google button signs people in, and the server makes their accounts for them.

broke.title: Keep the service history
broke.body: After a power loss, I found the older logs had already gone. I increased the history the server keeps so I have more to read after an interruption.

credits: Everything else: set up, wired together and run by me

serviceRecord.purpose: Movies, downloads and sign-ins, all on one small computer. Five pooled drives look like one folder to every device.

receipt.title: Same file. Faster read.
receipt.text: I changed one drive setting and tested it both ways. Network reads went from 32 to 70 MB/s, then back to 34 when I undid it. The change made the difference.

serviceRecord.care: Keep the logs as well as the movies. They are the service history of the machine.

back.pitch: The house has its own little machine room. It serves the movie library, runs about 40 apps and keeps 48 TB of storage in one place.
cut: One sign-in button for family and friends.
A storage pool made from five separate drives.
